messages:
carmen: FYI — user reported clicking a suspicious 'invoice' link at ~09:12 and then entered credentials on the page. They reported immediately when they realized. Asking for triage and containment steps.
sec-bot: Created incident IN-2026-042. Added playbook: phishing-user-click. Starting automated enrichment. Detected domain invoices-redwood[.]com.
sam: Can you paste the raw headers and the exact URL? Also which user (redacted) and when was their last successful SSO auth?
alice: I already kicked their SSO sessions and forced a password reset per the immediate response guide. Also toggled their service tokens to disabled. Will confirm KMS access next.
carmen: Pasting headers + link (sanitized):
```
From: billing@invoices-redwood.com
To: user@example.com
Subject: URGENT: Past due invoice
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:11:02 -0700
Received-SPF: none (mailfrom)
Message-ID: <msg1234@invoices-redwood.com>
```
Link: https://invoices-redwood.com/secure?id=ABCD1234

Sandbox results (attached run):
```
Verdict: MALICIOUS
Score: 72/100
Behaviour: credential-harvester -> fake-login.html
Network: attempted POST to https://collector[.]bad/creds
Artifacts: harvested_form_fields.csv
```

sec-bot: Sandbox confirmed credential-harvesting form. Recommended actions: 1) global block of invoices-redwood.com 2) immediate password + MFA reset for user 3) rotate any exposed API keys/service tokens 4) audit KMS access for that user's principals.
sam: Blocked domain at perimeter and added to blocklist rules. Also added a WAF rule to drop requests containing /secure?id=. Reduced one user-owned project role from owner -> maintainer pending review.
oncall: Ran an audit-log query for that user's activity window (09:00-09:30). Found 3 API calls to infra-management that look like config fetches at 09:18. Exporting logs to s3://redwood-incident-exports/IN-2026-042/logs.json for SOC.
alice: Checked KMS CloudTrail entries: no Decrypt/GenerateDataKey requests tied to the user's session after we revoked it. There were a few ListKeys calls from an infra service account earlier in the morning; will rotate any keys where the service token was implicated.
carmen: Notifying app owners and CS about possible customer impact. Drafting brief disclosure and guidance for affected customers.
sam: Adding IOCs to email scanner and spamhaus feeds. Also creating an automation ticket to run sandbox scans on attachments and links for incoming external emails flagged 'invoices' or with payment language.
oncall: Can we add an observability check to alert if any service account with high privileges is accessed from a recently disabled user? Might help detect chained access.
sam: Good idea — I'll open a ticket for infra to add that alert and tighten RBAC on CI/CD service accounts.
alice: Post-incident actions (proposed): 1) org-wide phishing refresher + targeted training for the impacted team; 2) enforce suspicious-link sandboxing on inbound mail; 3) review and tighten RBAC on service accounts and owner roles; 4) add KMS access verification step to runbook; 5) update runbook with explicit audit-log export path.
carmen: Agree. Also recommend a short comms note for product teams about what to tell customers if they ask.
sec-bot: Incident IN-2026-042 marked as mitigated. Follow-ups scheduled in the incident tracker.
_notes: generated by dataset generator: realistic slack thread about a phishing report, contains headers, sandbox output, containment steps, KMS/RBAC/audit log mentions
